newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia '97 net grain output may slip to 63 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia '97 net grain output may slip to 63 mln T.

text.p: Russia's net grain harvest in 1997 may slip to 63.0 million tonnes from last year's poor 69.3 million, Interfax news agency quoted the Russian agricultural research institute as saying on Tuesday.

It quoted a document from the Institute of Agricultural Information and Technical-Economic Investigations as saying that a reduced area for winter grains, which have higher yields than spring crops, could push down net output.
The institute said net wheat output could slip to 32-33 million tonnes from 1996's 34.9 million.

Russia planted 12.6 million hectares to winter grains for harvesting this autumn, below the 13.8 million sown for the 1996 harvest, the institute said, adding that autumn land ploughed for spring sowing was nearly four million ha below year-ago levels.

The institute also expressed concern over low fertiliser supplies, insufficient moisture levels, the late onset of spring and forecasts of a cooler summer, but did not specify which regions could be affected.

Interfax did not say whether the institute was government-run or independent of the Agriculture Ministry, but quoted the body as saying that unspecified "economic factors" could influence final grain output figures.
The government has said it aims to stabilise grain output in 1997 at a net 70.0 million tonnes.
Russia produced a net 63.4 million tonnes of grain in 1995. Both the 1995 and 1996 harvests are the worst on record in three decades.

The farm lobby, hungry for government subsidies and hand-outs and full of dire warnings, recently lost its most powerful government advocate, Alexander Zaveryukha, who lost his job as deputy prime minister in charge of the harvest in the recent Kremlin reshuffle.
